A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–H. The reformatting and added checklist in v2 do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original maze experiments measuring spectral decay, approximation errors, goal-reaching accuracy, and sample efficiency.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix H, including the maze evaluations and estimator comparisons.

M1.justification: The shifted successor measure, empirical transition-based estimator, truncated nu-SVD, TD updates, and greedy evaluation procedures are retained. Revised notation clarifies existing procedures without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the Medium, U, Large, and four-room maze environments, including non-uniform data collection. Non-tabular extensions remain proposed future work in both.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons remain the same, including ordinary versus measure-weighted SVD in Appendix H.3 and TD versus model-based estimation in H.4. Additional literature citations introduce no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported environments, discounts, exact and relaxed accuracy metrics, trajectory lengths, and sample-efficiency settings are retained. These include rank 40 for Medium/U-maze and rank 60 for Large-maze. New parameter-selection advice does not document changed experiments.

E4.justification: Both contain the same rank/shift sensitivity studies, four-room structural analysis, non-uniform-policy analysis, weighted-SVD comparison, and TD/model-based comparison. V2's additional discussion introduces no new supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: The new NeurIPS checklist, item 7, identifies the existing shaded bands as standard deviations. V1 already displayed shading and reported five seeds and averaging over random goals, but did not specify the shading statistic. No increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 4(a)'s illustrative state-value map changes from summing the unshifted successor measure over both actions to maximizing over the current action after marginalizing the one-step-shifted measure. This represents a different displayed quantity. The accuracy, approximation-error, and sample-efficiency results and their reported trends are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the coherence expression by including maximization over states. Section 6 revises the goal-value identity to use the one-step-shifted successor measure and adds algebra explaining the relationship. The main theorem statements and Appendix A–G proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract sharpens the negative claim from the successor measure being 'not low-rank' to 'not approximately low-rank.' The four principal contributions and the conclusion about shifting improving low-rank representations and goal-conditioned performance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability discussion through Section 7: downstream optimization remains unresolved, i.i.d. sampling bypasses exploration, shifting loses local information, and transfer beyond tabular/SVD settings is uncertain. Section 6 adds joint rank/shift tuning advice. It also replaces 'policy improvement' with an 'optimal policy' assertion, creating tension with the new downstream-optimization caveat.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link in Section 6 and Appendix H, and the checklist states that supplementary code includes configurations and reproduction scripts. V1 lacks this access information. The existing single-CPU and within-a-day runtime disclosure is retained; external availability is not verified.

R1.justification: Related work now explicitly contrasts intrinsic dynamical structure with function-class-dependent rank frameworks, adding citations such as Jiang et al. (2017), Du et al. (2021), and Jin et al. (2021). Additional linear-MDP and effective-horizon references broaden context without replacing the main research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 edits the introduction and experimental exposition, separates Section 4 into result and discussion subsections, and adds limitations and checklist sections. It renames ξ as spectral irrecoverability and its reciprocal as recoverability. The overall research sequence and Appendix A–H organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts conference-style typesetting, changing the title/author block, typography, text density, and figure sizing and placement. Maze panels in Figures 4, 7, and 8 are redrawn with different colors and added colorbars. Most underlying plots and the proof diagram are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through explicit scope limitations, identification of uncertainty shading, code-access information, and clearer mathematical exposition. Its new 'optimal policy' wording in Section 6 is less careful than v1's 'policy improvement' statement and conflicts with the downstream-optimization caveat. Despite this weakness, the added qualifications and reporting clarity provide a limited net improvement.
